name: Dentist take-home whitening trays

lead: A dentist makes trays moulded to your teeth and supplies carbamide peroxide gel to wear at home. They whiten teeth gradually over days, and people use them as a gentler alternative to chair-side bleaching or to top up its results.

Carbamide peroxide releases hydrogen peroxide, which breaks down pigment molecules in the tooth; the custom fit keeps gel on the teeth and off the gums. Wikipedia describes shade gains of about 1 to 2 shades within several days and says home bleaching produces less sensitivity than in-office bleaching.

paras: Users wear the filled trays for a few hours or overnight, usually daily for a couple of weeks. Effects fade, and retreatment every six to twelve months is mentioned.

Sensitivity and gum irritation are the commonly reported effects, and poorly fitting trays often lead to chemical burns. Peroxide at 10 percent or more can damage tissue. Listed contraindications include age under 16, pregnancy, untreated decay or gum disease and exposed dentine.

angle.text: Custom take-home trays hold dentist-supplied peroxide gel against your teeth, whitening them gradually at home with a visible gain over days. They are generally gentler on sensitivity than in-office bleaching.

lead: Dentist take-home whitening trays are custom-fitted trays, made from an impression of the teeth, that hold peroxide gel against the teeth while worn at home. Carbamide peroxide, which releases hydrogen peroxide on contact with water, is the usual agent [1].

Wikipedia reports that trays worn overnight or for 2 to 4 hours daily may lighten teeth by 1 to 2 shades within about three days, and that home bleaching causes less sensitivity than in-office bleaching [1]. Custom trays reduce leakage, and poorly fitting trays often lead to chemical burns [1].
No clinical studies are summarised here because none were available in the material gathered for this entry.

paras: Wikipedia credits Dr William Klusmeier with introducing custom tray bleaching in the late 1960s [1]. In 1989 Haywood and Heymann published support for custom trays, with carbamide peroxide favoured for a shelf life of one to two years versus one to two months for hydrogen peroxide [1].

Trays are described as worn overnight or for 2 to 4 hours daily, with 1 to 2 shades lightening reported within about three days [1]. Stains can return within a few months, and brushing or rinsing after food and drink, flossing and avoiding staining foods for 24 to 48 hours are among the maintenance steps listed [1].

Sensitivity is reported with whitening generally, and potassium nitrate and fluoride toothpastes ease it without evidence that they prevent it permanently [1]. Peroxide at 10 percent or more can damage gum tissue [1].

In the EU, retail products are limited to 0.1 percent hydrogen peroxide, with up to 6 percent allowed under professional supervision [1]. The US FDA is cited as endorsing gels under 6 percent hydrogen peroxide or up to 16 percent carbamide peroxide [1].
No studies found for this specific product category in the material gathered for this entry.

timeline.event: Custom tray bleaching introduced by Dr William Klusmeier.[1]
Haywood and Heymann publish support for custom trays.[1]
